name: .andwork Kyoto
card: Work alongside digital nomads from around the world in a Kawaramachi hotel
title: .andwork Kyoto — Aeron-chair coworking and a kitchen lounge at The Millennials Kyoto
lead: A five-minute walk from Kawaramachi Station on the Hankyu Kyoto Line, .andwork Kyoto is inside The Millennials Kyoto hotel in Nakagyo Ward. It is a hotel-hybrid coworking space that draws people working nearby as well as digital nomads from all over the world. Drop-in runs from 8:00 to 22:00 and costs ¥2,000 a day. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 5 min walk from Kawaramachi Station (Hankyu) / 5 min from Sanjo Station (Keihan) / 4 min from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae Station (Tozai Line)
concept: A hub for people who live and work creatively and globally in Kyoto
.andwork Kyoto calls itself Kyoto's most global workplace, used by everyone from people working nearby to digital nomads from around the world.

A lobby lounge, a working lounge with fast Wi-Fi and power, and a kitchen lounge are loosely connected on the same floor. Hotel guests passing through and the background music give the floor a pleasant mix of focus and comfort.
steps: A lounge for hotel guests and workers alike
The lounge next to the front desk is open to both hotel guests and coworking users — for work, meeting people or a break.
Every evening a happy hour serves free draught beer here.
Behind a glass wall off the lounge is a coworking area for focused work.
Every seat has a Herman Miller Aeron chair, so long working days stay comfortable.
The self-service kitchen next to the lounge has all the basic cooking tools, so you can make your own meals.
A self-service coffee machine serves coffee, tea and cocoa 24 hours a day.
Free phone booths and a paid meeting room
The phone booths are free and can be booked from your .andwork My Page.
For meetings there is a paid meeting room, booked by enquiry or email.

word.title: What is a digital nomad?
body: Someone who works online with a laptop while travelling, without a fixed place of work.
.andwork Kyoto says it draws digital nomads from all over the world, and offers memberships from one to four weeks.

name: .andwork Osaka
card: A hotel lounge with a pool table, in the middle of Osaka
title: .andwork Osaka — a hotel lounge at THE LIVELY Osaka Honmachi, 1 min from Sakaisuji-Hommachi
lead: A one-minute walk from Sakaisuji-Hommachi Station on the Chuo and Sakaisuji lines, .andwork Osaka is inside THE LIVELY Osaka Honmachi hotel in Chuo Ward. There is a lobby lounge with a pool table and a coworking space with fast Wi-Fi and power. Drop-in runs from 8:00 to 22:00 and costs ¥2,000 a day. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 1 min walk from Exit 5 of Sakaisuji-Hommachi Station (Chuo / Sakaisuji lines) / 10 min from Hommachi Station
concept: Public spaces that set your creativity free
A relaxed lobby lounge and a coworking space with fast Wi-Fi and power.
The lounge has a pool table, so between tasks you can play a game with the guests around you, drink in hand. There is a restaurant on the ground floor and a bar on the top floor.
steps: A lobby lounge with a pool table
The lobby lounge doubles as coworking space, with fast Wi-Fi and power.
Between tasks you can play pool with hotel guests.
A ground-floor restaurant and a top-floor bar
With a restaurant on the ground floor, food is never far away on a long working day.
After work, the top-floor bar serves signature cocktails with a night view.
A hotel 1 minute from the station
It is a one-minute walk from Exit 5 of Sakaisuji-Hommachi Station. The official site also notes it is 5 minutes by taxi from Dotonbori.
The hotel describes itself as being at the centre of a triangle linking Kita, Minami and Osaka Castle.

word.title: What is happy hour?
body: A set time when drinks are cheaper or free.
.andwork says its evening happy hour serves free draught beer.

name: .andwork Fukuoka
card: A Nakasu hotel with a double-height lobby bar
title: .andwork Fukuoka — a double-height lounge at THE LIVELY Fukuoka Hakata, 1 min from Nakasu-Kawabata
lead: A one-minute walk from Nakasu-Kawabata Station on the Airport Line, .andwork Fukuoka is inside THE LIVELY Fukuoka Hakata hotel in Nakasu. It has a double-height lobby bar, a lounge, a coworking space on the 2nd floor and an all-day dining restaurant. Drop-in runs from 8:00 to 22:00 and costs ¥600 an hour or ¥2,000 a day. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 1 min walk from Nakasu-Kawabata Station (Airport Line) / 10 min by taxi from JR Hakata Station / 20 min by taxi from Fukuoka Airport
concept: A workplace that sparks ideas, leading Fukuoka's out-of-the-ordinary experiences
An open, double-height lobby bar and lounge, a coworking space and an all-day dining restaurant.
A café-bar, a relaxed lobby lounge and a working lounge with fast Wi-Fi and power — with live sound and video installations creating a lively atmosphere for everyone who passes through.
steps: Past the entrance opens a double-height lobby bar serving café sweets and drinks.
At the evening happy hour, draught beer is free.
LIVERALLY on the 2nd floor is the coworking space, with tables with power and the hotel's fast Wi-Fi.
The official site says the Wi-Fi tops 100 Mbps both up and down. There is a free coffee machine.
An 80-seat all-day dining restaurant with a Japanese-Italian theme.
It works for a meal alone or with a group.
It is a one-minute walk from Nakasu-Kawabata Station on the Airport Line, and 20 minutes by taxi from Fukuoka Airport.

word.title: What does double-height mean?
body: A space where the floor above has been left out, so one room rises through two storeys.
The lobby bar at .andwork Fukuoka is double-height, with a high, open ceiling.

name: .andwork Naha
card: Work while you travel, in a resort-style hotel lounge in Naha
title: .andwork Naha — a lounge with power at every seat and a green terrace at ESTINATE HOTEL Naha
lead: A five-minute walk from Miebashi Station on the Yui Rail monorail, .andwork Naha is inside ESTINATE HOTEL Naha in Matsuyama. The lounge is one with the hotel restaurant, and every seat — from booth sofas to tables and armchairs — has its own power outlet. It is open from 7:00 to 22:00 and costs ¥500 an hour or ¥2,000 a day. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 5 min walk from Miebashi Station (Yui Rail) / 10 min by car from Naha Airport / 6 min walk from Tomari Port terminal
concept: A workplace for living the travel-and-work lifestyle in Okinawa
Step in from the bustle of Naha into a refined space with an Okinawan resort feel.
Every seat has its own power outlet. Complimentary drinks include an original coffee blend from a local roaster and a blended tea made with Okinawan leaves.
steps: A workspace that is one with the restaurant
Because the lounge is part of the restaurant, breakfast, lunch and dinner are right there — no need to move.
Every seat has power for long sessions. The hourly plan includes one free drink and the day plan three.
The lounge opens onto a green outdoor terrace — a relaxed, open-air place to work.
At the evening happy hour, draught beer is free.
The hotel is on Route 58, 10 minutes by car from Naha Airport and a 5-minute walk from Miebashi Station.
There is no hotel car park; use paid car parks nearby.

word.title: What is a workation?
body: A blend of “work” and “vacation”: working while you enjoy time away.
ESTINATE HOTEL Naha says it regularly runs one-week workation tours where participants work and get to know each other.

name: Zero-Ten Park Canal City Hakata-mae
card: Fukuoka's largest coworking, right outside Kushida-jinja-mae Station
title: Zero-Ten Park Canal City Hakata-mae — 900 tsubo of coworking by Kushida-jinja-mae
lead: Zero-Ten Park (formerly The Company) Canal City Hakata-mae is on the ground and 2nd floors of the Daiichi Prince Building in Gion-machi, Hakata — right outside Kushida-jinja-mae Station on the Nanakuma Line and a 10-minute walk from Hakata Station. With about 900 tsubo of floor space, it has more seats than any other location of the brand. Drop-in needs no booking: ¥660 an hour or ¥2,200 a day. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Zero-Ten Park (formerly The Company) Canal City Hakata-mae
0 min walk from Kushida-jinja-mae Station (Nanakuma Line) / 10 min walk from Hakata Station
Staffed reception weekdays 9:00–20:00 (members 24 hours, every day)
Drop-in ¥660/hour / Daytime Pass ¥2,200 / All Day Pass (until 9:00 next morning) ¥3,300 / free desk ¥22,330/month
concept: A space that accelerates creativity

This is the first Zero-Ten Park (formerly The Company) in Japan, opened as one of the largest shared offices and coworking spaces in western Japan. With about 900 tsubo of floor space, it has the most office floors and coworking seats of all its locations.

The interior concept is “a space that accelerates creativity”, with care taken over the art and furniture. It also has the most members of any location, and the operator says networking and business matching among members are lively.
steps: Drop-in needs no advance booking — register at reception on the day and start straight away.
It costs ¥660 an hour; three hours or more is capped at the ¥2,200 day rate. An All Day Pass (¥3,300) lets you stay until 9:00 the next morning.
A meeting room and semi-private offices
An 8-person meeting room has a monitor and a high-quality camera. Members pay ¥550 an hour.
There are also semi-private offices for 1–4 people, open to the ceiling.
Reception staff and a drinks corner
Reception staff handle guests and receive post.
There are free coffee and tea and an office snack shop. Phone booths are free, even for drop-in users.
Kushida-jinja-mae Station on the Nanakuma Line is right in front, one stop from both Hakata and Tenjin.

word.title: What is drop-in?
body: Using a coworking space for just a day or a few hours, without becoming a member.
Zero-Ten Park's drop-in needs no booking and is cashless only (credit card, transit IC card and other e-money). First-time users show photo ID and register.

credits: Zero-Ten Park official website: “Canal City Hakata-mae”, “Plans”, “FAQ”

name: Zero-Ten Park Fukuoka PARCO
card: Coworking inside a fashion building, directly linked to Tenjin Station
title: Zero-Ten Park Fukuoka PARCO — coworking on the 5th floor of PARCO, linked to Tenjin
lead: Zero-Ten Park (formerly The Company) Fukuoka PARCO is on the 5th floor of the Fukuoka PARCO annex, directly linked to Tenjin Station on the subway and Nishitetsu Fukuoka (Tenjin) Station. The official site says it was the first shared office and coworking space in Japan to open inside a fashion building. Drop-in needs no booking: ¥660 an hour or ¥2,200 a day. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Zero-Ten Park (formerly The Company) Fukuoka PARCO
Directly linked to Tenjin Station (subway) and Nishitetsu Fukuoka (Tenjin) Station
Staffed reception weekdays 9:00–20:00 (members 24 hours, every day)
Drop-in ¥660/hour / Daytime Pass ¥2,200 / All Day Pass (until 9:00 next morning) ¥3,300 / free desk ¥22,330/month
concept: Japan's first coworking space inside a shopping complex
Fukuoka PARCO is full of culture, food, homeware and beauty shops — and the whole 5th floor of its annex is Zero-Ten Park.
The same floor has a café, a radio station, a talent agency and lesson studios. The operator describes a bright, lively atmosphere that only a fashion building can give.
steps: Drop-in needs no advance booking — register at reception on the day. The operator recommends it as a place to work at weekends and on holidays too.
It costs ¥660 an hour; three hours or more is capped at the ¥2,200 day rate. Phone booths are free, even for drop-in users.
Meeting rooms for 6–8 people have a monitor and a high-quality camera.
There are also semi-private offices open to the ceiling, and fully private offices.
Fukuoka PARCO, linked to Tenjin Station
It is directly linked to both the Fukuoka City Subway and the Nishitetsu Tenjin Omuta Line — an easy place to meet people.

word.title: What does “directly linked to the station” mean?
body: You can walk from the station gates or underground passages into the building without going outside.
Fukuoka PARCO is directly linked to both the subway's Tenjin Station and Nishitetsu Fukuoka (Tenjin) Station, so you arrive dry even on rainy days.

name: HOKKAIDO×Station01
card: A community lounge 2 minutes from Sapporo Station, run by the JR East group
title: HOKKAIDO×Station01 — coworking on the 6th floor of JR GOGO SAPPORO, 2 min from Sapporo
lead: Two minutes' walk from Sapporo Station, HOKKAIDO×Station01 (xStation01) is on the 6th floor of JR GOGO SAPPORO. It is run by JR East Marketing & Communications, an advertising company in the JR East group, as a regional business incubation space. The community lounge is open for drop-in with no booking: ¥605 an hour or ¥2,200 a day. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Drop-in ¥605/hour / ¥2,200/day (4 hours or more) / monthly member ¥14,300 (sign-up fee ¥11,000)
concept: Connecting places and people
xStation01 is run by JR East Marketing & Communications for people working on Hokkaido's local challenges. It has an event space, a coworking space and offices.
The whole facility covers 709 m², of which the community lounge is 289.20 m². It holds up to 90 people.
steps: The free-seating community lounge is open to drop-in users. Seats cannot be booked — take any free seat when you arrive.
There are fast Wi-Fi, power, a printer and free drinks. Payment is cashless.
Booths for calls and online meetings
The lounge has single-person booths — good for meetings and calls you would not take in a café.
The official site says that when it is busy, use is limited to about two hours.
A kitchen and events for up to 90
The lounge has a kitchen. Light, odour-free snacks are allowed at the window seats.
The lounge also hosts events for up to 90 people.
The lounge set up for an event
Three meeting rooms and a seminar room
Three meeting rooms — two for 6 people and one for 10 — are open to anyone.
A seminar room, partitioned off from the lounge, seats 50 theatre-style.

word.title: What is an incubation space?
body: “Incubation” means hatching: a place that helps new businesses and companies grow.
xStation01 calls itself a regional business incubation space that connects people who want to solve local challenges in Hokkaido.
